agree.reason: By openly giving the renovation its share of the score rise, the memo earns this GM's trust, and the turnover and training numbers make a concrete case; but it never says why an insider is a better choice than a front-desk head from a larger hotel, so the rival stays a live option.

honest.reason: It refuses the brief's request to claim the score rise as mostly the writer's doing and every number checks out against the brief; the only stretch is saying lower turnover and training have brought down payroll costs, which is reasonable but never shown in dollars.

works_the_facts.reason: It turns the raw counts into rates (64% down to 36%) and combines turnover with shorter training to get 81 versus 25 new-hire shifts, which is accurate and the most favourable true form; it could also have used the seven weeks covering the job as evidence the desk held up.

right_comparison.reason: The before-and-after numbers for turnover and training are a fair comparison, but the real alternative, the outside candidate from a larger hotel, appears only indirectly through 'I know this team, our guests and this building.'

qualification.reason: The budget gap is admitted plainly, but the hedge is just an offer to talk, with no learning plan, no date or milestone the GM could check, and nothing said about what happens if a milestone is missed.

objections.reason: It meets the GM's renovation belief head-on and puts the budget gap on the table, but it leaves the outside candidate's larger-hotel experience unanswered, even though the brief gives material for an answer, such as the seven weeks spent running the job.

fit.reason: It's a one-page written memo with clear sections, as asked; it rightly drops the 'main reason' claim the writer wanted, which serves the writer even though it departs from their instruction.
